title: CRM Marketing Manager
description:
Headquarters: Armenia
URL: http://cxmdirect.com

Description

CRM Marketing Manager

Reporting to: CMO
Location: Fully Remote
Markets: 12

About the Role

We are looking for a CRM Marketing Manager to own CXM’s customer lifecycle marketing across 12 markets. You will use customer data, segmentation, automation, and personalised communications to improve activation, first-time deposits, retention, reactivation, and customer lifetime value.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can build CRM journeys from the ground up, manage campaigns across multiple markets, and use performance data to continuously improve results.

Key Objectives

  • Build and launch at least 3 automated lifecycle journeys covering welcome/activation, retention, and reactivation within the first 6 months.
  • Improve the current 9% lead-to-FTD conversion rate through targeted CRM activation campaigns.
  • Support reducing churn to below 10% through structured retention and reactivation programmes.
  • Build and maintain localised CRM journeys across all 12 markets.
  • Maintain 99%+ deliverability and ensure all CRM activity meets applicable compliance requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Lifecycle & CRM Strategy

  • Own customer journeys across onboarding, activation, conversion, retention, loyalty, VIP, churn prevention, and win-back.
  • Define triggers, audiences, journey logic, exclusions, frequency caps, and exit criteria.
  • Coordinate email and push communications to create a consistent customer experience.

Campaigns & Automation

  • Build, launch, and optimise automated CRM campaigns using platforms such as Mailgun, Braze, Klaviyo, or equivalent.
  • Create targeted campaigns based on customer behaviour, lifecycle stage, market, language, and product.
  • Manage promotional campaigns, newsletters, VIP communications, retention campaigns, and partner communications.
  • Develop and maintain reusable email templates and content blocks.

Segmentation & Personalisation

  • Build and maintain customer segments, consent lists, exclusions, and communication rules.
  • Configure personalised and dynamic content based on customer data.
  • Work with Product, Analytics, and IT to define and validate data and event requirements.
  • SQL knowledge is a strong advantage.

Localisation

  • Manage CRM communications across multiple languages and markets.
  • Coordinate translation, editing, and linguistic QA.
  • Ensure correct currencies, dates, links, variables, legal messaging, tone, and RTL requirements.
  • Maintain master journeys and localisation matrices across all markets.

Deliverability & Compliance

  • Monitor deliverability, bounces, spam complaints, suppression lists, and domain/IP reputation.
  • Maintain strong email hygiene and deliverability standards.
  • Run detailed pre-launch QA covering audiences, links, variables, tracking, content, sender details, and scheduling.
  • Ensure campaigns comply with consent, unsubscribe, data retention, and local regulatory requirements.

Analytics & Optimisation

  • Analyse CRM performance by market, language, segment, and customer lifecycle stage.
  • Measure conversion, retention, churn, revenue, and incremental uplift — not just opens and clicks.
  • Run A/B and holdout tests across offers, messaging, timing, frequency, channels, and journey structure.
  • Maintain a clear optimisation backlog and turn insights into measurable improvements.


Requirements
  • Proven experience in CRM, lifecycle marketing, email marketing, or marketing automation.
  • Hands-on experience building automated customer journeys.
  • Strong understanding of segmentation, personalisation, triggers, and lifecycle strategy.
  • Experience managing CRM across multiple markets and languages.
  • Strong knowledge of email deliverability and campaign QA.
  • Experience with Mailgun, Braze, Klaviyo, or similar CRM platforms.
  • Strong analytical and data-driven mindset.
  • Comfortable working with technical and data teams.
  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to manage multiple campaigns simultaneously.
  • Experience in FX, fintech, trading, igaming, or another regulated B2C environment is highly desirable.
  • Able to work independently in a fully remote environment.

Ideal Candidate Background

The strongest candidates are likely to be currently working as a:

  • CRM Manager / Lifecycle Marketing Manager
  • Email Marketing Manager
  • Marketing Automation Specialist
  • Retention Marketing Manager
  • CRM-focused Digital Marketing Manager

Experience with high-volume B2C customer journeys, FTD/conversion funnels, retention, reactivation, and regulated markets will be particularly valuable.



Benefits

What We Offer

  • Fully remote working with minimal meeting overhead.
  • Ownership of CRM across 12 international markets.
  • Genuine opportunity to build and improve the customer lifecycle function.
  • An established business with the resources and budget to execute ambitious CRM initiatives.
  • Freedom to test, learn, and implement new ideas.
  • Competitive, above-market compensation.
  • KPI-linked bonus connected directly to CRM and business performance.

Recruitment Process

Stage 1: HR interview — experience, motivation, and fit.
Stage 2: CMO interview — CRM expertise, strategy, and relevant experience.
Stage 3: CEO interview, where required.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/cxm-direct-crm-marketing-manager

title: Agency Partner Manager
description:
Headquarters: Germany (Remote) ; Ireland (Remote); Netherlands (Remote) ; Portugal (Remote) ; Spain (Remote) ; United Kingdom (Remote)

Who we are

Typeform is a refreshingly different form builder. We help over 150,000 businesses collect the data they need with forms, surveys, and quizzes that people enjoy. Designed to look striking and feel effortless to fill out, Typeform drives 500 million responses every year—and integrates with essential tools like Slack, Zapier, and Hubspot.

Typeform is fully remote by design. For this role, we can hire candidates based in the UK, Ireland, Germany, Portugal or The Netherlands

About the role

We’re looking for an Agency Partner Manager to own and scale Typeform’s Agency Partner Program. You’ll build revenue generating relationships with marketing, digital, research, customer experience, and professional services agencies, helping them create valuable solutions and client offerings using Typeform.

A key part of this opportunity will be Research Flow, our AI moderated research platform. Research Flow combines qualitative depth with quantitative scale, enabling teams to design studies, recruit participants, run adaptive conversations, and generate insights in hours. You’ll help agencies incorporate these capabilities into their services and bring new research solutions to their clients.

This is a hands on commercial role where you’ll recruit and activate partners, support their continued growth, and drive net new revenue across their client base. You’ll join the Partnerships team and work closely with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product, and Partner Operations.

What you’ll do

  • Own the Agency Partner Program from recruitment and onboarding through enablement, activation, and ongoing partner success.
  • Build strong commercial relationships with agencies that can extend Typeform’s reach and create new solutions for their clients.
  • Help partners package Typeform and Research Flow into services across customer research, market research, lead generation, marketing, and customer experience.
  • Drive net new MRR through agency sourced and agency influenced opportunities, working with Sales and Customer Success on shared accounts and co selling activity.
  • Set and manage quarterly objectives across revenue, partner activation, and program growth.
  • Partner with Marketing on shared campaigns, webinars, case studies, content, and other demand generation activity.
  • Refine partner segmentation, tiers, incentives, and reporting to create a program that can scale efficiently.

What we’re looking for

  • five or more years of experience in partnerships, channel sales, business development, or agency management.
  • A track record of generating revenue through agency or services partners.
  • A strong understanding of marketing, digital, research, or professional services agency models.
  • Experience building partner programs and processes that can scale without significant manual oversight.
  • Strong commercial judgement and confidence managing revenue, pipeline, forecasting, and partner performance.
  • Excellent relationship management and communication skills, with the ability to align stakeholders across different teams.

Nice to have

title: Head of Technical Support @ Koast.ai
description:
Headquarters: Tampa, Florida
URL: https://koast.ai

Head of Technical Support | Full-time | Remote (US hours) | Reports to the CEO

Koast is the AI operating layer for teams that run Meta ads at volume. Agencies, in-house media buying teams, and enterprise buyers managing 10+ ad accounts and launching 50+ ads a week use Koast to launch faster, automate optimizations off real attribution data, and see every account from one Command Center. The Koast Agent is the next layer: an AI that reads the account, spots what matters, and acts inside guardrails.

Our customers are media buyers. When something breaks, it is not a support ticket to them. It is a campaign that did not launch, a budget that did not move, or an account they cannot see. They need someone on the other end who has run ads, knows what they are looking at, and can tell the difference between a Meta API error, a user mistake, and a real bug.

That is this role. You are the anchor between our customers and our engineers. You will onboard every new account, own every ticket, QA every release before it hits production, and make sure engineering hears about patterns, not anecdotes.

What You WIll Own...

Onboarding. Every new customer gets set up right the first time: ad accounts connected, attribution (Hyros, Cometly) wired in, team invited, first launch done together on a call. You will run these sessions yourself, then build the playbook and the in-app flow so the next hundred customers need less of you.

Support, end to end. Intercom is yours. Response times, resolution quality, the help center, the macros, the escalation path. You will answer tickets yourself until the volume justifies a hire, and you will know every customer by name before you delegate a single one.

Triage and the bridge to engineering. You decide what is a bug, what is a feature gap, what is Meta being Meta, and what is user error. Bugs get reproduced, documented with steps and account context, and filed in Shortcut with enough detail that an engineer can fix it without asking you a follow-up question. Patterns get surfaced in the weekly review with numbers: how many customers, how much spend affected, how often.

QA and release quality. Nothing ships to production without you having run it against a real ad account. You will own the QA pass on every release: launch flows, automations, Agent actions, integrations. You know what a broken campaign structure looks like in Ads Manager, and you catch it before a customer does.

System tightness. Meta API connections, token refreshes, webhook health, Whop account provisioning, attribution syncs. You will monitor them (Sentry, PostHog, internal dashboards), notice when something drifts, and get it fixed before it turns into a ticket.

Customer health and retention. You will know which accounts are launching, which have gone quiet, and which are about to churn. You will bring that list to the CEO weekly and you will own the outreach.

What you will do week to week

  • Run onboarding calls for new customers and enterprise accounts. Connect accounts, verify data, launch the first campaign together.
  • Work the Intercom queue. Own first response, resolution, and follow-up.
  • Reproduce every reported bug against a real ad account before it goes to engineering.
  • File and prioritize Shortcut tickets with repro steps, account IDs, screenshots, and expected versus actual behavior.
  • QA each release candidate against a test account and a live customer scenario. Sign off or send it back.
  • Monitor Sentry and PostHog for errors and drop-offs. Flag anything that affects more than one customer the same day.
  • Run the weekly support review: ticket volume by category, time to resolution, top three patterns, customers at risk. One page, numbers first.
  • Write help center articles and Loom walkthroughs for anything you have explained more than twice.

What sets you apart

  • You have run Meta ads. You know Ads Manager, campaign and ad set structure, learning phase, Advantage+, pixel and CAPI setup, and what "the API rejected my creative" actually means. This is a hard requirement, not a preference.
  • You have done support or customer success for a B2B SaaS product and you were the person engineers trusted because your bug reports were correct.
  • You can QA software. You have written test cases, run release checks, and sent a build back because it was not ready.
  • You are calm with a frustrated customer whose launch just failed, and you are direct with an engineer who shipped the thing that failed it.
  • You write tightly. Your tickets, your help articles, and your customer replies are shorter than everyone else's and clearer.
  • You want to build the support function, not just work inside one.

Requirements

  • 3+ years in customer support, customer success, or technical support for a B2B SaaS product, including at least one role where you were the primary bridge to engineering.
  • Hands-on Meta ads experience. You have managed ad accounts, launched campaigns, and troubleshot Ads Manager and API issues. Agency or performance marketing background strongly preferred.
  • Experience with Intercom or a comparable support platform, and a ticketing or project tool (Shortcut, Linear, Jira).
  • Experience running QA or UAT on software releases.
  • Comfortable reading logs, API responses, and error monitoring (Sentry or similar). You do not need to write code. You need to read enough to know where the problem is.
  • Familiarity with attribution tools (Hyros, Cometly, Triple Whale, Northbeam) is a plus.
  • Available full-time during US business hours.

How You Work

Small team, high autonomy. Decisions are made with numbers, written down, and revisited when the numbers change. These are the values we run on. If they sound like you, you will fit right in.

  • Mastery. "Good enough" is where you start, not where you stop. You keep sharpening the craft: tighter repros, faster resolutions, fewer repeat tickets.
  • Push the Boundaries. You take on the ambitious version of the problem. Most support teams answer tickets. You want to build the one that prevents them.
  • Embrace the Challenge. When a customer's launch breaks at 9pm, you are in the thread, not waiting for the morning standup.
  • Responsibility. You own your commitments. If a fix slips, the customer hears it from you first, with a new date attached.
  • Dedication. You dive into the hard, unglamorous problems (an intermittent API error, a broken sync nobody can reproduce) and iterate until they are solved.
  • Collaboration. You write clearly, share what you learn, and make engineering and sales faster for having worked with you.

Why Koast

  • Early-stage impact. You will be one of the first ten full-time employees. The support function, the onboarding playbook, and the QA standard will be the ones you built.
  • AI and ads at scale. You will support some of the highest-volume ad teams on Meta and see what an AI agent does with real budgets every day.
  • Real compensation. Full-time salary, performance bonuses tied to retention and resolution metrics, and paid time off. Bootstrapped and profitable, so the seat is stable and the growth path is real.
  • Remote and flexible. Work from anywhere, on your schedule, during US hours. Just make sure every customer is launching.

How to apply

Record a Loom, five minutes or less, covering these four things in order:

  1. Explain why you're a fit. Screen-share and explain projects youve worked on, ad accounts you have had access to (blur what you need) or companies you helped before. Walk us through the structure and tell us the last thing that broke in it and how you fixed it.
  2. One bug report. Take us through an example of a report you filed that an engineer fixed without asking you a follow-up question. Tell us how you reproduced it.
  3. One angry customer. A time a customer was losing money because of a product issue. What you said in the first reply, what you did next, and what happened.
  4. Where Koast fits. Sixty seconds on what breaks first when a media buyer starts managing 20 accounts from one platform instead of Ads Manager, and how you would catch it before they do.

Email the Loom link and your LinkedIn or resume to jobs@koast.ai with the subject line "Retention is king".

NOTE: DO NOT APPLY IF YOU HAVE NO EXPERIENCE WITH PRODUCTS LIKE THIS / ADVERTISING / CANNOT WORK US HOURS.

No cover letters. We watch the Loom first and read the resume second. Applications without the video are not reviewed.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/koast-ai-head-of-technical-support-koast-ai

Confirmed Product Analyst - Demand
description:
About BlaBlaCar

BlaBlaCar is the world’s leading community-based travel app enabling 27 million members a year to carpool or travel by bus in 21 countries. Our team of 800 employees counts over 50 nationalities and is spread across our 5 global offices, 30% working fully remotely.


Your mission
Our Data department is organised following Data Mesh principles, distributing data ownership to cross-functional and domain-specific teams that manage, own, and serve the data as a product.
The Data Demand team’s mission is to help BlaBlaCar grow as a global OTA through data, covering the full customer journey from brand and product discovery through marketing and landing pages, to search, booking, post-booking, and payment. As the team expands its scope from self-service towards decision intelligence, we want to strengthen our ability to proactively analyse member, marketplace, and product behaviours, and to influence the decisions that shape the product.
As a Data Analyst, you will join the Data Demand team to drive decision-making through data: framing the right questions with stakeholders, going deep into data to explain what is happening, sizing opportunities, interpreting experiments, and translating insights into actionable recommendations for Product and Marketing teams.
Your responsibilities
Partner with Product, Marketing, and Business stakeholders to understand their goals, frame analytical questions, and identify the decisions where data can have the highest impact.
Collaborate with Data Engineers, Data Scientists, and other Data Analysts to improve the quality, usability, and coverage of our data products, and explore opportunities to turn advanced analytics or ML/AI initiatives into measurable business impact.
Lead end-to-end analyses on product and business topics such as marketplace dynamics, search-to-book performance, member behaviour, audience knowledge, or CRM and marketing impact.
Go beyond dashboards to investigate the “why” behind trends, anomalies, and performance changes, combining exploratory analysis, statistical reasoning, and strong business context.
Build clear narratives from data: communicate findings, trade-offs, confidence levels, and recommendations in a way that helps stakeholders align and act.
Contribute to reusable business knowledge and context engineering by documenting insights, analytical frameworks, or business relationships, and play a governance role in aligning definitions, reducing gaps between teams, and improving data quality over time.
Leverage BlaBlaCar’s available GenAI tools to work more efficiently in day-to-day analysis and documentation, while applying strong critical thinking to challenge, validate, and contextualise the outputs before using them in decision-making.
Your qualifications
Master’s degree or equivalent: engineering school, business school, etc
At least 3 years of professional experience working as a Data Analyst
Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience analysing large and complex datasets.
Good understanding of product analytics, funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation, experimentation, and performance monitoring.
Ability to structure ambiguous problems, challenge assumptions, and translate business or product questions into robust analytical approaches.
Experience with data visualisation, with a strong sense of how to design clear, trustworthy, and decision-oriented outputs.
Solid communication skills: you can turn analysis into a compelling story, adapt your message to different audiences, and influence decisions with clarity and humility.
Comfort working with cross-functional teams and building strong stakeholder relationships.
Curiosity for product, growth, marketplaces, and member behaviour, with a pragmatic mindset focused on impact over perfect analysis.
Python or another analytical programming language, causal inference, or advanced experimentation knowledge is a plus.
Fluent in English 
If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications outlined above, tell us why you’d still be a great fit for this role in your application!
What we have to offer
Hybrid: 2 to 3 days at the office for this role
4 additional weeks on top of legal maternity/paternity leaves
50% healthcare coverage (Alan)
Financial support for home office equipment
Minimum 25 days holiday per year 
Local meal plan policy (Swile card)

Personal growth via trainings, mentorship, and internal mobility programs
Employee Stock ownership plan
